messages:
Anya (PM): Quick sync: ACME wants a pilot for "micro-pools" with "soft guarantees" — predictable tail latency during short spikes. Need product + eng alignment on what we ship and what we call an MVP.
Samir (Eng): +1. Do we mean soft guarantees as in bounded P95 under a burst window, or billing-level promised headroom?
Anya (PM): Both, ideally. Customer wants deterministic latency for short bursts (30-90s) but isn't ready to commit to full reserved pricing. So proposal: small committed baseline + burst credits with SLA on latency when credits available.
Liz (SRE): Operationally we need clear autoscale timeouts and graceful fallback. If we promise latency during a 60s spike, autoscaler must prewarm or we need KV/prefix caching to keep tail latency low. Otherwise we overpromise.
Ken (Solutions): From ACME convo: they care about user-perceived latency on chat flows. They gave an example: bursts of 200 concurrent sessions for ~45s during events. They want <300ms P95 token latency for the first 64 tokens.
Marta (CS): ACME POC says they'd accept a small pilot credit pool instead of long-term commit. They want a clear failover path if guarantees fail.
ACME POC: Confirming — pilot ok as long as we shadow for 2 weeks and we have an outage playbook. We can't accept big billing surprises.
Samir (Eng): For the pilot we can implement a tenant_soft autoscale mode. Rough config suggestion:
```
autoscale:
  mode: tenant_soft
  prewarm_seconds: 20
  burst_window_seconds: 60
  cool_down_seconds: 30
  reserve_headroom_pct: 12
```
That gives short prewarm and a reserved headroom to reduce cold-start P95.
Liz (SRE): Need metrics: token_latency_p95, cold_start_rate, prewarm_success_rate, burst_credit_balance. Also alerting: token_latency_p95 > 350ms for 5m -> page.
Ken (Solutions): We should also define billing model for burst credits: e.g., X credits per minute of burst per vCPU equivalent, carryover disabled for pilot. Keep it simple.
Anya (PM): Proposed launch gates for pilot: (1) Observability — dashboards and alerts in Console, (2) Autoscale config support and default, (3) Customer-facing SLA language for pilot (soft guarantee + rollback), (4) Oncall playbook and escalation, (5) Clear billing estimator + usage cap.
Samir (Eng): Implementation tasks: API flag to enable micro-pool tenancy per customer, autoscale mode + prewarm path, burst-credit ledger, and telemetry tags. I can prototype in the runtime repo; need 2 sprints for stable rollout for pilot.
Marta (CS): I'll prepare a one-page pilot agreement and onboarding checklist (billing cap, test plan, success criteria).
Liz (SRE): Ops runbook notes: if token_latency_p95 spikes after prewarm, fallback policy = route to compatible model variant (lower mem) + notify customer. We need a graceful degrade path in code.
ACME POC: Sounds good. We also want a demo with synthetic spike test before the pilot goes live.
Samir (Eng): Agree — add a stress harness in staging that can replay 45s 200-conc sessions. I'll add a k6 script and a simple load generator.
Anya (PM): Decisions now: autoscale mode = tenant_soft (pilot), prewarm 20s, burst window 60s, billing = pilot credits with cap, launch gates as listed. Action items: Samir -> prototype + stress harness, Liz -> dashboards + alerts, Marta -> pilot agreement + customer comms, Ken -> create demo script with ACME, Anya -> draft pilot SLA and internal launch checklist.
Ken (Solutions): I'll schedule a dry-run demo with ACME next Tues.
Samir (Eng): I'll open PRs for API and runtime flags and add the example config to docs.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: runtime/micro-pools/prototype -> staging. Build 0.3.7 -> started.
Anya (PM): Cool. We'll reconvene after the staging dry-run. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
